title: "The Directed Acyclic Graph"

# The Directed Acyclic Graph

After this page you can draw a tiny Git history as a graph and say what a branch is.

## Snapshots with parents

A **commit** is a snapshot of the whole project at one instant, plus metadata (author, message, time) and a pointer to the commit that came before it — its **parent**.

Two commits in a row:

```text
A  ←  B
```

`B`’s parent is `A`. Time flows left to right in this book’s diagrams; the parent pointer points backward, toward history.

A chain of commits is a **directed acyclic graph** (DAG): directed because each commit points at parents, acyclic because a commit cannot be its own ancestor.

## A branch is a name

A **branch** is a movable name for one commit. `main` is a file that contains a hash. When you commit, Git writes a new snapshot whose parent is the current tip, then slides the name forward.

```text
A  ←  B  ←  C     main
```

`main` now names `C`. `A` and `B` are still there. Nothing was overwritten.

## A second line of work

Start a branch named `feature` while `main` is at `C`, then add two commits:

```text
A  ←  B  ←  C          main
            ↑
            D  ←  E    feature
```

`C` has two children. Git is fine with that. A **merge commit** has two parents:

```text
A  ←  B  ←  C  ←  M     main
            ↑     ↑
            D  ←  E     feature
```

`M` ties the two lines together. **Rebase** (chapter 9) copies `D` and `E` onto a new parent instead. New hashes, similar diffs. You will do that after first-repository muscle memory is in place.

## HEAD

**HEAD** is “where I am.” Most of the time it points at a branch name, and the branch name points at a commit:

```text
HEAD → refs/heads/main → C
```

Commands that “move HEAD” are moving that name, or (when HEAD is **detached**) pointing HEAD at a raw commit hash. Detached HEAD shows up when you check out a tag or a hash. New commits on a detached HEAD are easy to lose when you switch away. Create a branch before you leave, or find them later with the reflog (chapter 17).

```bash
git log --oneline --graph --all
git rev-parse HEAD main
git status
```

`git status` says `HEAD detached at …` when it is.

## Look at the graph

Once you have a repository (next chapter’s neighbor, chapter 3):

```bash
git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all
```

`--decorate` prints the names (`main`, `HEAD`, tags) next to the commits they point at. The graph is the truth. Commands add objects and move names. If you hold the graph, `reset`, `rebase`, and `reflog` stop feeling like magic.
